meta.title: Card details modernized
meta.text: The open card view has been rebuilt on the shared design system while keeping every visual and interaction exactly as it was. You see no change when you open a card, answer a question, or reply in the conversation. This work modernizes the internal architecture so all of Seismic's views use consistent tokens and patterns, making future refinements faster and more reliable.
chapters: A planned card and the queue

meta.title: Canvas icons: every emoji, more icons, in colour
meta.text: A canvas can now carry any emoji or one of about three hundred Lucide icons, instead of a short fixed list. The canvas dialog opens on Icons, which you can search by name and draw in one of ten colours. The Emoji tab is a full emoji picker with categories, search and skin tones. The chosen icon shows in its colour on the canvas tabs.

meta.title: Cards the chat creates show as cards
meta.text: When you ask Seismic's chat for a new task or idea, the card it creates now shows in its own bubble under the reply, with the card's live cover: its state, labels and progress, as the canvas shows them. One click opens it. Before, the chat only said in words that it had created the card, and you had to find it on the canvas.
chapters: The new card in its own bubble

meta.title: View switcher clears the canvas tabs
meta.text: On medium-width windows the Canvas | Parked | Table switcher used to sit in the centre and overlap the canvas tabs at the bottom right. It now sits at the left, one row above the bottom row, stays on top of full-page views like Parked, and shrinks to icons for the views not showing when space is tight.

meta.title: Larger pause marks
meta.text: The pause symbol shown on a workstation held for restart is now as large as the circles beside it, so the row reads evenly.

meta.title: Running code reviews count as at work
meta.text: The Workstations pill at the bottom of the canvas says how many agents are at work. A card whose code review agent was busy used to count as idle there. Now the reviewing agent counts while it actually works, and drops out again once the review is done or paused for a restart.
chapters: Two cards waiting, none at work

meta.title: Merges in planning show both cards, joined
meta.text: While an agent plans the merge of two cards, both cards now stay on the canvas joined by a solid purple line with an arrowhead at each end and a solid merge mark on it. Each card shows the merge icon and says its own state followed by the merge status, such as "Planned · Planning merge", in purple. Once the merged card is ready, both cards read "Merged · review" after their state and stay joined. Before, the link was faint and only the left card showed a grey status.

meta.title: Cards that could not land say so
meta.text: When approved work cannot land because the main checkout has uncommitted changes to the same files, its card now reads "Not landed (file conflict)" instead of "Demo ready". It shows that way on the canvas, in Needs you and at the top of the opened card, so it is clear at a glance that the card needs you to fold those changes in.
chapters: The card says why it did not land
What to do is on the card

meta.title: Top bar stays usable while a card is open
meta.text: Opening or creating a card used to dim and blur the whole screen, including the top bar. Now only the canvas below the bar dims. The menu, search, help, chat and user buttons stay sharp and clickable.

meta.title: Seismic's remaining views on Tailwind
meta.text: The last parts of Seismic that still used the old hand-written stylesheet now use the same component styling as the rest of the app: card faces, plans, the canvas's rings and hints, the queue, the archive, the plan sheet, the merge view, the chats and the dialogs. Nothing is meant to look different. The point is one consistent, maintainable styling system, in light and dark, on desktop and phone. This tour shows each of those views as it looks now.
chapters: Hover, waits and the play button
A queued card and its chain
The plan sheet and its doc

meta.title: Plan cards no longer share on approval by default
meta.text: On a plan's cards, approving no longer publishes the demo to the team's demo site unless the owner has ticked "Share on approval". Other cards behave as before.

meta.title: Open cards keep clear of side sheets, the menu and the inbox
meta.text: An open card no longer hides the Chat, Needs you, Agent work or project settings sheets: it narrows to fit beside them. It also never covers the left menu or the inbox's list, even when these are opened or pinned while the card is already open. On a window too narrow for all of them, the sheet lies over the card's right edge and stays fully usable.

more.title: Sheet controls stay usable with an open card
more.text: Settings, Agents and Needs you remain accessible while a card is open. Open a sheet, switch between them, or close it without losing the card conversation.
chapters: Close the sheet and keep the card

meta.title: Diff tab: file bars when space is tight
meta.text: When the Diff tab is too narrow to show the file tree next to the code, the two now stack. The changed files sit at the top in a bar that opens and closes the tree. Below it, each changed file is its own bar that opens or closes its changes, and picking a file in the tree opens its bar and scrolls to it. With enough room, the tree stays beside the diff as before.
chapters: Pick a file in the tree

meta.title: Switches sized for a finger on touch screens
meta.text: On a phone, the "Share on approval" switch under the Approve button was the size made for a mouse pointer, so a thumb often missed it. On touch screens, every on/off switch is now larger and its whole row, the words included, takes the tap. A tap that lands a little beside the switch now flips it at the first try. On a computer nothing changes.

meta.title: A new phone view: one project at a time
meta.text: The phone view is being rebuilt around one project at a time. A slim top bar names the project and switches it, and it stays in place when a card is open. A box shows how many agents are at work and on which cards. The project's cards follow in sections (Queued, Planned, then Parked and Done), twenty at a time. A floating bar at the bottom keeps a new card within reach of the thumb. For now the new view is a preview under ?view=phone-next, next to the current phone view.

meta.title: Merges update themselves when a card changes
meta.text: When two cards are being merged and either changes before the merge is approved (an edit, or the in-progress card's agent handing over), the comparison now runs again by itself. While it runs, the previous result stays visible but dimmed, and approval waits for the new result. Before, approving refused with a message to separate the cards and merge them again by hand.

more.title: Merges recover cleanly after edits and deletion
more.text: Merge comparisons wait for changes to settle, and an old approval refusal disappears when the comparison updates. Deleting either card separates the pair, so restoring a deleted card brings back its original task without reviving the old merge.

more.title: Each merge settles independently
more.text: A merge compares again after its own cards stop changing, even while other workers keep updating the board. Separate merging pairs have independent delays, so a busy project no longer leaves a changed merge waiting indefinitely.

more.title: A changed merge shows as updating at once
more.text: When either card of a merge changes, the comparison result on screen is dimmed under "Updating: a card changed" right away, and Approve merge is disabled. The new comparison still starts a few seconds after the last change, so a burst of edits makes only one. An out-of-date result can no longer be approved during that wait.
chapters: Updating the moment a card changes

more.title: Keep the previous comparison after an update fails
more.text: When an updated merge comparison fails, the earlier result stays dimmed and readable beside the error. Try again preserves it until a successful comparison arrives, while approval stays disabled.

more.title: Earlier follow-ups keep their original questions
more.text: When a card’s questions change, its earlier merge comparison keeps showing the questions it originally proposed. Those questions remain readable through a failed update and retry, until a successful comparison replaces the preview.
chapters: Retry replaces the question only on success

meta.title: Phone: full-page chat and card search
meta.text: On the phone, Seismic's chat is now a full page instead of a sliding panel, with chat history, the field and the microphone. A new search page finds the project's cards by title or code. Back from a found card returns to the same results.
chapters: Open a card from the results

meta.title: Phone: menu sheet and a Needs you page across projects
meta.text: On the phone, the menu opens as a full-height sheet with Needs you and your projects, and tapping a project switches the whole view to it. The bell opens a Needs you page that gathers what waits in every project, each entry naming its project and offering one-tap replies. Opening a card from another project switches the top bar to it; browser Back returns to the page and the card's cross lands on that project's list.

meta.title: Many workstations fit the status bar
meta.text: With many workstations on one machine, the row of dots in the status bar used to grow wider and wider. Now six to twelve workstations go into two rows and thirteen to eighteen into three, so the pill keeps the bar's height. From nineteen on, a single bar shows how many workstations are at work, waiting for the owner or free, as coloured shares. Hovering the pill still lists every workstation and its card.

meta.title: Manual code reviews on pull-request projects
meta.text: Projects that send approved work out as a pull request can have each card's work code reviewed too. With code reviews set to "Manually, at handover", a purple "Start code review" button appears next to "Approve (PR)" when the agent hands over. A click starts the review before the pull request opens, and while it runs, approving warns that the review is still going.
chapters: A project that lands through pull requests

meta.title: Distinct shapes for review severity
meta.text: Review counts now distinguish severity by shape as well as colour. Light bulbs, circles, squares and diamonds make the levels easier to recognize, with double diamonds for critical findings and a white exclamation mark for blockers. Existing colours are preserved in both light and dark themes.

meta.title: Needs you hides the floating bar on the phone
meta.text: In the phone view, the Needs you page is a full page, and the floating bar along the bottom now steps aside while it is open. Closing the page with its X or Back brings the bar back. This matches how chat, search and open cards already behave.
chapters: The bar on the home list
Needs you is a full page

meta.title: Newest plans first, snoozed plans last
meta.text: The mobile Planned list shows active tasks first and snoozed tasks at the end, newest created first within each group. This order also applies across Load more, so newer snoozed tasks cannot push active work onto a later page.
chapters: Active work stays on the first page
Snoozed plans remain at the end

meta.title: Warning toasts in yellow, with buttons below the text
meta.text: When you start a card that has to wait for another one, Seismic shows a warning that it is queued and hasn't started yet. That warning used to be a brownish box with its buttons squeezed in beside the text, so the text wrapped into a narrow column. Now it uses the same yellow as the other warnings in the app: the text runs across the full width, and 'Go to card' and 'Dismiss' sit below it.
chapters: Before: a brown box, buttons beside the text
After: yellow, text full width, buttons below

meta.title: Follow-up review status
meta.text: When a follow-up code review runs, the card shows its numbered review check in teal with an activity animation. This makes it clear that the reviewer is still checking the work.

more.title: Follow-up review checks
more.text: Follow-up code reviews show their numbered status as soon as the check is due. The same status appears on compact cards, so the review round remains clear in search and other lists.

meta.title: Slash menus are solid now
meta.text: Typing a slash in a card description or the message box opens a menu: cards to link, or an agent's skills. These menus used to be almost transparent, so the text beneath them showed through and mixed with their entries. They now look like every other dropdown in Seismic: a solid surface with a border and rounded corners, so each entry reads cleanly.
chapters: Before: the menu lets the text show through
After: the card-link menu is solid

meta.title: Expanded card no longer overlaps the project switcher
meta.text: An open card used to reach up under the project switcher and the floating pills on short windows. It now always starts below them, so those controls stay visible and clickable.

meta.title: Working lines and dots move without repainting
meta.text: Cards with an agent at work show a line drawing itself at their foot, and the workstation dots in the status bar pulse. These animations used to make the browser repaint the card on every frame, which made cards shimmer on a zoomed-out canvas. They now only slide and fade, which the browser does without repainting, and they look exactly as before.

more.title: Workstation dots pulse faster, with less rest
more.text: The dots in the status bar for workstations with an agent at work now pulse a third faster and rest at full colour only briefly before fading again, so the activity reads at a glance.

meta.title: Questions get their own Answer button
meta.text: When an agent asks a question, the owner can now submit the answer with a button inside the question itself, instead of using the send arrow in the blue box below. The button shows up once an option is picked and sends the picks with any remark typed.

meta.title: Staged changes in the way of a landing can be folded into the card
meta.text: When approved work can't land because the main checkout has uncommitted changes to the same files, the card offers to fold those changes into its branch. Changes that were only staged used to be missed, so the card offered nothing even though the message promised it would. Now staged changes, staged deletions included, are named on the card, and the card shows as needing you. The failure appears as a yellow warning that stays on screen, with a Go to card button to get back to the card.
chapters: Before: the toast promises a fold that never comes
Before: no offer on the card
After: a yellow warning with Go to card
After: the card offers to fold the change in

meta.title: Skills now carry the seismic: prefix
meta.text: The agent skills Seismic gives its workers are renamed from the old obeya: prefix to seismic:. For example, obeya:settings becomes seismic:settings. Every brief, doc and card text that names a skill uses the new name, including the skill lists given to Codex and Antigravity workers.

meta.title: Resume a merge from either card
meta.text: Opening either original card brings you back to the merge already in progress. The current comparison, prepared result and approval controls remain available after visiting another card.
chapters: Before: the return link loses the comparison
After: return to the current merge

meta.title: Question indicators follow the theme
meta.text: Collapsed conversations show a dot when an agent has an open question. The dot follows the interface’s waiting color in light and dark themes, with hover text explaining the cue. Tasks, ideas, proposals, and demo handovers all share the same behavior.

meta.title: Agent process sweep tells reused pids apart
meta.text: On Linux, agent process identities now include the kernel boot id alongside the start time in clock ticks. A recycled pid in a restarted container is no longer mistaken for a recorded agent process.

meta.title: Project settings that drill into sections
meta.text: The project settings sheet on the right is now a list of sections with an icon each: Allowed commands first, then Agents and models, Auto suggestions, Development environment, Code reviews, Git and releasing, Card archiving and Demos. Each slides into its own view, with a repository switcher where a project has several repositories, and every change applies at once. New commands from a repository show a red count until they are reviewed, settings that restart a repository's agents ask before they are saved, and a project can be archived from the foot of the list.
chapters: Agents and models: a restart asks first

more.title: Project settings on the phone
more.text: On the phone, the button at the left of the floating bar opens the project's settings: the same list of sections and views as on the desktop. The logo at the top left opens the same left menu as on the desktop, with what the phone has a view for. A repository setting the configuration refuses shows why, with Try again, and changes not saved yet stay when the settings are closed and opened again.
chapters: The desktop menu at the top left

more.title: Settings keep their page and pending clone values
more.text: Phone settings and Needs you switch directly through the menu, with Back returning to the project. Clone details survive a trip back to the settings list. If a workstation save is refused, Try again repeats the pending changes, and sharing waits until the visible settings are saved.
chapters: Clone values survive a trip back to the list
Retry includes the refused workstation changes

meta.title: A canvas is empty when nothing on it is visible
meta.text: Every card now knows whether its canvas holds it, folded away or not. A canvas can be deleted only when nothing visible is on it. Archived cards, ended plans and parked cards no longer get in the way, and the drawer, the server and Seismic agree on that. An archived card whose canvas was deleted comes back on main, at a free spot.
chapters: Archive the last card, delete the canvas
Back from the archive, onto main

meta.title: Finish working changes with an editable task
meta.text: Seismic suggests completing unfinished repository changes and saves their complete patch separately from the task description. The description stays editable even for large captures, and the agent receives the saved changes on its own machine. Repositories with changed submodules are excluded because a parent patch cannot carry that work.
chapters: A short task, with its captured changes kept separately
Seismic proposals match in the inbox
Submodule work is not offered as a complete capture

meta.title: A three-step welcome to Seismic
meta.text: On the first start, Seismic now walks you through setup in three steps, shown by a progress bar: agents, recommended features, and your first project. You pick one or more agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; Pi is coming soon), and each one shows what it needs on your machine. A callout above the button says how many agents are ready, and the next step lists the features that can wait, with a warning when you skip some.

more.title: Later setup steps need a configured agent
more.text: In Seismic's three-step welcome, the later steps can only be reached once at least one agent is configured, also through the progress bar. Unpicking every agent disables the way on until one is picked again, and the Ready badge on each agent now also takes git into account.
chapters: No agent, no way past it

meta.title: Setup notices logins done in a shell
meta.text: When Seismic starts for the first time, its setup assistant shows which agents and tools are logged in. Until now it only checked again when you came back to the page, so a login done in an SSH shell or another terminal was never noticed. Now the list checks again every 15 seconds while a login on the current step is missing, also where Seismic cannot open a terminal itself. Every login also has a "Check again" button that checks right away.

more.title: Check again shows a check in progress
more.text: While the setup assistant checks the machine, by a click on "Check again" or by its automatic check every 15 seconds, the button is disabled and shows a spinner with "Checking". Checks run one after another, so the list always ends on the latest answer.

meta.title: Onboarding keeps a usable default agent
meta.text: The setup assistant now tells Seismic which agents are configured when the first project is created. If Claude Code isn't one of them, the project's default agent becomes the first configured one, so the first task started without a choice runs instead of failing. Machines with Claude Code behave as before.

more.title: Plain folders only for agents that can use them
more.text: Codex and Antigravity work only inside a git repository. When a project's agents run in one of them, Seismic no longer offers to use a folder without git: setup and the configuration show a short note on why and offer to set up git instead. With Claude Code, both options remain.

meta.title: Open cards blur the floating controls
meta.text: When a card expands, the floating controls under the top bar and the status bar blur together with the canvas, while the top bar stays sharp. A large card can take up the space those controls held, top and bottom, and cover it, so long cards get more room. Closing the card brings everything back.

meta.title: Parked cards in a grid
meta.text: The Parked view now lays its cards out in a grid instead of one long column. Large screens show three cards per row, medium screens two, and phones one, so more parked work is visible at once.

meta.title: A Table view of the project's cards
meta.text: Besides the canvas and Parked, a project now has a Table view: every card on any canvas and each plan workstream as a row, with state, priority, canvas, plan, group, category, complexity and last update. Any column sorts with a click, in each value's own order, and a toolbar searches titles and filters by state, priority and canvas. A click on a row opens the card just as it opens on the canvas. The view is part of the address, so a link or a reload comes back to the table.

meta.title: Table view follows the address
meta.text: Opening a project with ?view=table already showed the Table view, but following links or pressing Back/Forward inside the open project ignored it. Now the view follows the address: Back returns to the table, and a card link with ?view=table closes onto the table instead of the canvas.
chapters: A card link with the table

meta.title: Separator in the status bar
meta.text: The bottom status bar now has a thin, subtle vertical line between the Workstations pool and the usage limits. It has some space above and below, and only shows when both are visible. This makes the two groups easier to tell apart at a glance.

meta.title: A way out when a card's model runs out of usage
meta.text: When the model behind a card runs out of usage, the card now says so and names the model. From the card you can try again once usage is added, hand the work to a different model with "Select new agent", or, for a code review, skip the review and approve without it. Handing the work to another model of the same tool keeps the agent's session, so nothing is lost. Choosing a different model for a code review applies to that card only, so a review that ran out no longer leaves the card stuck.
chapters: Hand the work to another model
A code review out of usage

more.title: Usage limits show the model and keep it on retry
more.text: Cards identify the worker or reviewer that hit a usage limit, even before its session opens. Try again keeps the code review on the same model, including when the reviewer was selected just for that run.
chapters: A worker can hit its limit before opening a session
A review can show the account default
Try again keeps the selected reviewer

meta.title: See which dependencies still hold a card
meta.text: When you open a planned card, the callout links to the unfinished cards connected to it by dependency arrows. The list updates as prerequisites finish and clears once they are all done.
chapters: Before: the remaining dependency was missing
After: the card names every unfinished prerequisite
The callout clears when the last prerequisite is done

meta.title: Start fresh or resume a recent chat
meta.text: Open Seismic’s right-hand chat more than 20 minutes after you last opened it and it starts fresh with five dated shortcuts above the composer. Select a shortcut to resume that session, or start typing to clear the shortcuts. Clicking New chat opens an empty composer immediately.

meta.title: Create cards inside a group
meta.text: Double-click empty space inside a group’s shaded boundary to add a card to that group. The card opens for editing at the spot you clicked. Double-click outside the shading to create an ungrouped card.
chapters: Before, the card cuts a gap in the group
Double-click inside Checkout to add a card
Create an ungrouped card on the open canvas

more.title: The second tap picks the group
more.text: When a double-tap crosses a group’s shaded boundary, the new card follows the second tap. That point determines both where the card lands and which group it joins.
chapters: Before, the first tap picked the group
The card now follows the second tap

meta.title: Antigravity usage limits in the status bar
meta.text: When Antigravity is installed and signed in, Seismic's status bar now shows how much of its plan's usage limits is used, next to the Claude and Codex meters. A click lists every limit Antigravity reports, per model group, with when each one resets. The numbers refresh every minute and reading them uses none of the quota.
chapters: A third meter in the bar

meta.title: Code review items stay with a card, and fixes go straight back to the reviewer
meta.text: Once a code review has run on a card, its items and their history stay with the card through every later handover, also on projects that only review on request. Before, the agent's next handover dropped the whole list, so the following review started from nothing and never checked whether the fixes held. Now a handover with fixes sends them straight to the reviewer, which checks each one and marks it fixed or reopens it with its reasons, while new findings continue the numbering.
chapters: Before: a review started by hand
Before: the handover wipes the list
After: the same card, with the fix
After: the fix goes straight to the reviewer

meta.title: Named defaults for agents and chats
meta.text: Model and harness pickers now show the actual names with a Default badge on the matching row. You can see what a new task or chat will use and choose an alternative from the same menu.
chapters: Project settings mark the inherited harness
Start a task with a named default
A new chat shows its project model

more.title: Defaults follow settings changes
more.text: Project settings show the Default badge in the dropdown, leaving more room for the selected name. An open chat follows saved model settings, and a task choice marked Default follows the account’s current model.
chapters: A one-off start follows the account’s choice

more.title: Model defaults follow your settings
more.text: Choose the row marked Default to follow Configuration in project settings or the project’s model for a task. If the source model changes before the task starts, both pickers show the new name.
chapters: Return a project to the named default
Save the default for a task
Both pickers follow the new model

more.title: Harness changes preserve model choices
more.text: Returning a project harness to Default keeps its model and effort choices. The task picker shows the configured Claude model when you switch to Claude Code, and Submit to new agent opens with the project’s review settings.
chapters: Changing the harness keeps project choices
The task picker knows the Claude default
Review answers start from the review default

meta.title: Projects get their own icon or emoji
meta.text: Every project in the switcher used to carry the same branch symbol, so projects could only be told apart by name. Now each project can have its own icon or emoji, chosen beside its name in Configuration. The icons are a curated Lucide set that leads with software, business, buildings, people and sports, in a colour of the canvas palette. The emoji tab lists every system emoji with a tab per category.
chapters: An icon beside the project name
A colour from the canvas palette
Saved, and shown in the switcher

meta.title: Real harness logos in the usage pills
meta.text: The status bar shows how much of each AI coding tool's plan limits is used. Each pill now begins with that tool's own logo (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) instead of a hand-drawn stand-in and small meter, followed by each limit and its percentage. The percentage turns orange or red as a limit runs low, and a click still lists every limit with when it resets.

meta.title: Password warning during repository setup
meta.text: If Git needs a password for the repository check, setup shows an amber warning and explains that cloning may still work. The info button explains why the check cannot ask for a password. You can still choose Clone and create project to use saved credentials.
chapters: See why the check needs a password

more.title: Setup uses your Git SSH configuration
more.text: When you set up a project from an SSH repository, Seismic uses the SSH command Git selects to check access and clone. That lets setup use a configured identity or jump host.
chapters: Check an SSH repository with its configured identity
Clone with the same SSH transport

meta.title: The setup page shows at once, each check on its own
meta.text: On a first start, Seismic checks which coding agents are installed and signed in. The setup page now appears immediately, and each agent is checked in its own request, with a spinner beside its name until it answers. git, which every agent needs, is checked separately too, so a slow git never delays an agent's result. An agent you have not touched is ticked once it is found ready; one you ticked or unticked yourself keeps your choice. Each agent, and git, has its own Check again.
chapters: Before: one wait for every check
Now: the page at once, a spinner per agent
git is checked on its own
Ticked before the check: stays on
Each agent checks again on its own
Unticked before the check: stays off

more.title: A failed setup check can be retried
more.text: When Seismic can't finish checking an agent or git in the Setup dialog, it now says so right there and offers a Check again button for that check alone. Before, a check that failed the first time showed nothing to retry, so that agent was left unchecked. The agents you've ticked stay ticked while you retry.

meta.title: The canvas works from the keyboard
meta.text: On the canvas, Tab still opens the next card that needs you, and from any focused control it now moves on as it does everywhere else. Card faces and plan titles can be reached with Tab and opened with Enter or Space, and closing a card puts the focus back on it. The canvas tabs, their drawer and the Canvas / Parked / Table views all work without a mouse, and Space on a control does what that control does instead of starting push-to-talk.
chapters: Card faces and plans are reachable
Enter and Space open, focus comes back
The views in the push-to-talk row

meta.title: Usage bars on desktop and phone
meta.text: On desktop, thin bars beneath Session and Week show how much of each limit is used. At 95%, the fill turns red and the percentage keeps its usual color. Open the usage popover on desktop or phone to see larger bars beside each limit. The phone header keeps its compact percentages.
chapters: Larger bars in the usage popover

meta.title: Deleting a canvas no longer strands parked cards
meta.text: When you delete a canvas that still has parked or snoozed cards, Seismic now warns you with the counts and lets you pick which canvas they move to, main by default. A yellow button moves them and deletes the canvas; a grey one goes back. Canvases without such cards are still deleted straight away.
chapters: A canvas with parked and snoozed cards
Warning, target canvas and the choice

more.title: Retry a canvas deletion
more.text: When a canvas has parked or snoozed cards, choose where they should go before deleting it. The confirmation shows progress and keeps your choice if the request fails. After deletion succeeds, the cards return in separate spots on the destination canvas.
chapters: The cards return to separate spots

more.title: Live counts when deleting a canvas
more.text: The delete warning updates when parked or snoozed cards change, and your destination stays selected. If the counts change after you confirm, Seismic shows the updated totals and lets you confirm again.
chapters: The warning updates as cards arrive

meta.title: Manage connected harnesses
meta.text: Configuration now has a Harnesses page for connecting and disconnecting coding agents. The setup wizard verifies each connection before adding it. Agent menus and the usage bar follow the connections you’ve confirmed.
chapters: Keep only the harnesses selected during setup

more.title: Onboarding follows the harnesses you select
more.text: Onboarding uses the harnesses you select to set up your first project. If you choose only Codex, it becomes the sole connection and usage meter, even when an earlier preference named another harness.
chapters: Verify the connection, default, and usage

more.title: Harness settings reflect active connections
more.text: Harnesses shows when every available harness is already connected. After a disconnect, the project editor updates its Git requirement to match the harness that will run its workers.
chapters: Use a folder after disconnecting Antigravity

meta.title: Weekly usage visible in compact phone pills
meta.text: When several harnesses report limits, the phone shows compact usage pills. Each pill now lists every limit with a one-letter name (S for Session, W for Week) and a plain percentage, so the weekly limit no longer disappears when Session usage is higher. Harnesses that report only Session show just that. Tapping a pill still opens the popover with progress bars.

meta.title: Close cards from the Card actions menu
meta.text: The Card actions menu lives in the top-right corner of an open desktop card. Choose Close or press Escape while the menu is open to return to the canvas or Archive.
chapters: Find the menu in the top right
Press Escape with the menu open

meta.title: Relaunch Setup from Advanced
meta.text: Open Settings → Advanced and click Relaunch Setup under Reconfigure Setup. The dialog uses a solid surface so you can read the setup controls clearly. Your choices are saved when you click Confirm.
